column3: New theme: Junior Precious Metals Miners Rotation (4 stocks)
column4: Tickers: PPTA, FSM, NG, PAAS | Thesis: PPTA is trading higher on ongoing momentum from the opening of its U.S. Army-backed antimony pilot plant and related strategic loan/government support for the Stibnite project, which has re-rated the stock as a key critical-minerals play. FSM and PAAS are being bid up primarily on the back of stronger precious metals prices and bullish positioning ahead of upcoming production/earnings catalysts, with silver and gold miners broadly catching a bid as metals continue to hold elevated levels. Secondary support comes from positive analyst sentiment and technical strength in PAAS, plus Fortuna’s resource and portfolio-optimization news that improve medium-term cash flow leverage to metal prices.

column3: New theme: Net Lease Single-Tenant REIT Recovery (5 stocks)
column4: Tickers: ADC, EPRT, NNN, O, WPC | Thesis: The main catalyst this week is a broad risk-on move into rate-sensitive real estate and net-lease REITs following increasingly dovish Fed commentary and growing expectations for near-term rate cuts, which improves the relative appeal of long-duration, high-yield REIT cash flows. In that backdrop, the group is also getting a tailwind from solid recent earnings, dividend growth (e.g., NNN’s dividend raise and acquisition guidance) and tightening credit spreads that support valuation multiples and acquisition economics. There is no single stock-specific headline driving ADC, EPRT, NNN, O, and WPC individually; they are primarily rallying as part of a sector-wide re-rating of net-lease REITs tied to the changing rates narrative.

column3: New theme: Regulated Water Utility Infrastructure (4 stocks)
column4: Tickers: AWK, AWR, CWT, WTRG | Thesis: The main catalyst is the advancing all-stock merger between American Water Works (AWK) and Essential Utilities (WTRG), which has recently secured multiple key state regulatory approvals (Kentucky, Ohio, Virginia), increasing confidence the deal will close and driving a bid across the regulated water space. In addition, American Water’s stronger-than-expected Q2 2026 results, reaffirmed EPS guidance, and visible capital investment/regulatory pipeline are supporting sentiment and lifting peers via sector read-through. Broader rotation into defensives/low-beta utilities in a choppy tape is adding incremental demand for names like AWR, CWT, HTO, and WTRG.

column3: New theme: Private Equity & Alternative Asset Management Platforms (2 stocks)
column4: Tickers: ARES, HLNE | Thesis: ARES is trading higher this week primarily on a strong Q2 earnings print, with analysts highlighting robust growth in private credit and infrastructure platforms and raising forward forecasts and price targets (e.g., TD Cowen to $155, JPMorgan to $153, while maintaining bullish ratings). There is also a positive flow backdrop for alternatives after Ares raised roughly $8.5 billion for its latest specialty credit fund, reinforcing the growth and fee-earning AUM story. Broader risk-on sentiment in equities amid stable macro and earnings strength in large-cap tech is providing an additional tailwind to alternative asset managers like Ares.

column3: New theme: Management Consulting & Research Advisory Services (2 stocks)
column4: Tickers: HURN, IT | Thesis: HURN is trading higher this week primarily on the back of its record Q2 2026 earnings beat and raised full‑year guidance, which drove a ~35–40% post‑print jump and strong follow‑through as investors reprice the growth trajectory. The catalyst is a broad-based upside surprise: adjusted EPS well above consensus, double‑digit revenue growth led by digital/AI-enabled and managed services, and a higher 2026 EPS and revenue outlook signaling sustained demand and margin strength. Positive analyst commentary and renewed buy ratings are reinforcing the move, but they are secondary to the earnings/guidance shock.

column3: New theme: Technology Intellectual Property Licensing (2 stocks)
column4: Tickers: IDCC, DLB | Thesis: Dolby (DLB) is being driven higher by its latest quarterly earnings report, which showed an EPS beat versus consensus (around $0.69 vs $0.67) and strong Q4/full-year guidance despite a modest revenue miss. The move is amplified by unusually heavy volume and multiple momentum alerts as investors react to the 10‑Q and forward outlook. InterDigital (IDCC) has been supported by ongoing positive sentiment around its Amazon patent license agreement and broader licensing wins, but there does not appear to be a fresh, discrete news catalyst this week beyond positioning ahead of upcoming earnings and continued recognition of its royalty stream growth story.

column3: New theme: Mobile App Platform & Advertising Monetization (2 stocks)
column4: Tickers: BSP, APPS | Thesis: Digital Turbine (APPS) is moving higher this week primarily on the back of a strong Q1 print that beat Street expectations on both EPS and revenue, reinforcing the view that its growth inflection is underway. The move is being reinforced by ongoing positive sentiment around its app discovery/ad monetization flywheel and recent AI/data partnerships (e.g., Databricks, Google Cloud) that support a higher medium-term revenue trajectory. In short, the catalyst is an earnings beat plus growing confidence that its new AI-driven platform deals can sustain above-consensus growth.

column3: New theme: Technology Intellectual Property Licensing (2 stocks)
column4: Tickers: IDCC, DLB | Thesis: Dolby (DLB) is being driven higher by its latest quarterly report, where it beat EPS expectations ($0.69 vs. $0.67) despite a slight revenue miss and guided to stronger Q4 and full-year growth. InterDigital (IDCC) is moving on a very strong Q2 print and guidance raise, with annualized recurring revenue hitting a record ~$626M and the company lifting full-year 2026 revenue outlook by $85M at the midpoint, supported by its new Amazon streaming/license agreement and recent patent injunction wins against Disney. Both names are effectively trading on better-than-expected earnings outlooks and strengthened licensing economics.

column3: New theme: Industrial Process Equipment, Automation & Flow Control (3 stocks)
column4: Tickers: EMR, FLS, LECO | Thesis: The main catalyst pushing EMR, FLS, and LECO higher this week is strong industrial earnings and outlooks, led by Lincoln Electric’s record Q2 results and raised 2026 sales growth guidance, which are reinforcing confidence in the broader industrial and automation cycle. LECO reported double‑digit sales growth to about $1.22B, expanded margins, and a 13% increase in adjusted EPS to $2.93, while highlighting strengthening Americas demand, improving automation activity, and a record backlog, all of which support higher valuations across peer names. In addition, multiple upward price target revisions and “buy/overweight” ratings on LECO are adding momentum to the group and contributing to sector-wide rerating.

column3: New theme: Building Envelope, Ceilings & Interior Construction Products (2 stocks)
column4: Tickers: AWI, CSL | Thesis: Armstrong World Industries (AWI) and Carlisle Companies (CSL) are both trading higher primarily on the back of strong Q2 earnings from Carlisle that beat expectations on revenue, EPS, and margins, driving a relief rally across the building products space. Carlisle’s print featured record ~US$1.6bn revenue, double‑digit EPS beat, and a higher full‑year revenue growth outlook, which has pulled in buyers to related building envelope names. For AWI specifically, there is no stock‑specific newsflow this week beyond general sector sympathy to Carlisle’s results and broader risk‑on sentiment in cyclicals.

column3: New theme: Junior & Mid-Tier Precious Metals Miners Rotation (3 stocks)
column4: Tickers: SBSW, HYMC, AUGO | Thesis: SBSW is grinding higher mainly on continued bullish sentiment toward precious metals and a technical uptrend, with the ADR trading above key moving averages and supported by prior earnings strength and improving balance sheet narratives, rather than a specific new headline catalyst this week. HYMC’s strength is being driven by ongoing momentum from recent high‑grade gold/silver exploration results, a fresh position initiated by the Swiss National Bank, and positive technicals after its extended rally.
